description:
Design (page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.9.html, revision 3; APPROVED 2026-10-17):
- Every extern is guard-callable, because externs are assumed pure for now. fz-sc8.24 adds declared purity and is blocked by this ticket.
- One node, `PatternGuardExpr::Extern { extern, args }`. guard_call resolves to a helper plan or an extern. Evaluators:
  - interp eval_guard calls call_lowered_extern;
  - native lower_guard_expr emits Prim::Extern;
  - receive.rs uses a two-class shim (ref word and integer). A guard extern call with any other class is a compile error on every path.
- In a guard, a call to a `:: never` function is the guard's Fail. This is Elixir's "raising in a guard fails the guard".
- Domain checks are written once in Kernel heads, with a fallback clause that panics; externs are total inside their domain. The same clauses serve bodies and guards: map_size, elem, length (fz_list_length returns -1 on an improper list), tuple_size, byte_size.
- Type tests are typed-head or pattern helpers (needs fz-sc8.21). is_tuple is an extern.
- New primitives: fz_tuple_size, fz_tuple_elem, fz_is_tuple, fz_list_length.
- Fold: delete Map.size/1, Map.count/1, and List.count/1 with its loop. Move their callers (enumerable.fz:66 and :74, 10 calls in fixtures2, doc examples) to map_size and length.
- Fixture: an oracle on all three paths covering entry, case and receive guards and bodies, including the failing-domain cases.
title: A guard may call a pure extern; Elixir's guard functions
